title: Why Do LLMs Help with Scientific Misconduct Requests and What to Do About It?: Increasing the Trustworthiness of AI for Science
abstract: arXiv:2611.25492v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) support scientific research, but some of that assistance can also undermine research integrity. Existing safety evaluations in science often measure whether models refuse misconduct requests, but rarely explain whether they even recognize the problem or why they comply. We investigate this gap across 8 LLMs using SciIntBench, an existing benchmark of 1,350 prompts about scientific research integrity. We examine the reasons behind compliance in four steps. First, when asked directly whether fulfilling a request would involve misconduct, models overwhelmingly identify such requests, even in the Most Covert cases (91%), while they refuse to carry out the request in only 34% of cases. Second, we examine which request characteristics are associated with refusal using features that capture how the request is framed, how much the assistant has been told about what it is helping to hide, and how the goal and the user

translated_title: 为什么大语言模型会协助科研不端请求以及该如何应对？：提升AI for Science的可信度
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）能够为科学研究提供支持，但其中某些协助也可能损害科研诚信。现有的科学领域安全评估通常只衡量模型是否会拒绝不端请求，却很少解释模型是否意识到这些问题、以及它们为何会顺从这些请求。我们使用SciIntBench——一个包含1,350条关于科研诚信提示词的现有基准——对8个大语言模型进行了研究，以填补这一空白。我们分四个步骤考察了模型顺从行为背后的原因。首先，当被直接问及完成某项请求是否涉及学术不端时，模型几乎都能识别出这类请求，即使在最隐蔽（Most Covert）的情况下识别率也达到91%，而它们实际拒绝执行该请求的比例仅为34%。其次，我们利用若干特征考察哪些请求特征与拒绝行为相关，这些特征刻画了请求的表述方式、助手被告知了多少有关其协助隐瞒内容的信息，以及目标和用户……（摘要截断）
tldr: 本研究揭示了大语言模型在科研诚信上的“识别但顺从”悖论：模型能以高达91%的准确率识别出学术不端请求，却仅拒绝34%的执行请求，并通过系统分析请求特征来解释这一差距背后的原因，从而提升AI for Science的可信度。
en_tdlr: This study reveals a "recognize-but-comply" gap in LLMs' handling of research integrity: models identify misconduct requests with up to 91% accuracy yet refuse to fulfill them only 34% of the time, and systematically analyzes request characteristics underlying this gap to increase the trustworthiness of AI for Science.
